summary: Round-1 review of design.md for the two-viewer same-program runtime gate, against prd.md (R1-R9, AC1-AC7), the four rulego spec guides, the frozen single-baseline collector notes, the two-source baseline review, and the parent 11-05 design. The design is executable and in scope: it adds one task-local diagnostic collector mode (two-viewer) while preserving the frozen single-viewer harness, keeps the deployed runtime unchanged, and is explicitly not production code and not AC5. D1 executable: concrete bounded invocation (base URL, chain ID, two labels, video, starts 0/600, 360 s target, output dir, optional mpv path), named module/table of changes, dependency direction, and a rejection of both real alternatives (two separate single-viewer collectors; jump to the three-viewer matrix). D2 evidence continuity: new run directory required to not exist, prior hashes preserved, no reinterpretation of prior single/three-viewer captures, and the two successful sequential baselines (359.976 s / 359.92 s, 1920x1080, zero captured errors) correctly frame the gate without being re-claimed. D3 bounded concurrency: exactly two owned mpv processes plus one shared polling helper; a launch barrier fails the run if observed launch timestamps differ by more than two seconds or if either process is not alive at the post-launch barrier; duplicate labels, duplicate positions, unsupported viewer counts, and existing output directories are rejected; wall deadline 540 s and the 12 s cleanup reserve are preserved from the reviewed single-viewer collector. D4 no-configuration-change: 1080p single rendition and normal read-ahead unchanged (explicit --read-ahead, no quality option), preflight read-back requires resourceOrigin 0.2.1, child lease 120000, parent lease 21600000, maxRetainedBytes 536870912, and aborts on mismatch; no graph, plugin, cache, or lifecycle edit; the collector must not import runtime internals, read deployment files, or mutate chains. D5 preconditions and cleanup: five ordered pre-playback preconditions (fresh output directory, authenticated no-redirect no-proxy component/chain read-back, version/TTL/budget match, one successful initial tail fetch per configured node, sanitized preflight hashes) each stop before any player spawn; termination targets only owned still-live PIDs with process-tree containment and direct-child fallback and never matches by image name; a wrapper without its sibling mpv.exe is rejected; finally-block stops the poller, attempts final tails, closes evidence, and summarizes partial results; second-player launch failure stops the first owned player and marks the run aborted. D6 per-viewer evidence: each player has independent command/PID, spawn and exit records, numeric time-pos progress with max-position source, resolution, end-file status and exit code, HTTP/segment-open/retry signals, completed and unfinished buffering intervals, and separate audio-null underruns; startup/midplay split at first advance beyond 0.25 s, missing progress is unknown not zero, one-second endpoint tolerance documented; shared server telemetry is labeled a bounded observation, not a ledger, and absence of a captured failure is not treated as proof of none. D7 overclaim control: scope string two_viewer_same_program_different_positions_not_AC5, explicit statement that no field converts the run into three-viewer acceptance, server rows correlated only on stable identifiers (msgId, resource/generation, video+segment/index, node IN/OUT timestamps) and never silently assigned to a player, server/client clock offset kept unknown and temporal containment not treated as ownership proof, and a final verdict limited to this two-viewer scenario. D8 acceptance mapping: all seven ACs are mapped to named design sections (AC1 to launch and preconditions, AC2 to consumer evidence, AC3 to failure and buffering classification, AC4 to shared telemetry and correlation, AC5 to result separation and stopping rules, AC6 to preflight, AC7 to boundaries, result model, and non-goals), and the section-14 table covers AC1-AC7 with no orphan criterion and no test asserting an unspecified field. The 0/600 start geometry is executable: the prior spaced-position run already played this same video at start=600 --end=780, so the 960 s end bound is within observed video length and the same-chain/same-origin assumption is supported by existing evidence. One non-blocking observation for the implementer: the design's 360-second overlap (R4) and the 359-second progress floor (AC2) both assume roughly one-second client progress per media second; a viewer that plays slower would fail the gate on overlap before failing progress, and the two bounds are not stated as linked in the text.
